summary: Intermittent 429s after SSO token refresh cascade on Dedicated pool (route smoothing + burst pool misalignment)
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429 throttles observed after a scheduled SSO token refresh window. The errors spike for ~30–90s every ~15 minutes and primarily impact streaming/chat websocket sessions and short-lived batch embedding uploads.

Customer context: ShelfAI runs an orchestration layer that refreshes SSO-backed short-lived API tokens on a 15m cadence. They are on a Dedicated capacity pool with route smoothing enabled and a shared burst pool configured for low-latency streams. After a token refresh cycle, many worker processes reconnect in parallel and ShelfAI sees elevated 429s despite overall traffic remaining within tenant commit limits.
impact: Multiple production customer-facing features degraded: realtime chat sessions dropping, a small percentage (~8-12%) of batch embedding requests failing with 429s during refresh windows. Business impact: user-facing errors and retry amplification increases downstream latency and cost.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a client that obtains short-lived API tokens from SSO and schedules refreshes every 15 minutes with no jitter.
2) Start ~600 concurrent websocket sessions and ~200 short batch embedding uploads across 50 worker hosts.
3) Trigger token refresh simultaneously for all workers (simulate scheduled refresh).
4) Observe 429 rate increase on streaming endpoints and occasional 429s for batch endpoints for 30-90s post-refresh.
observed_behavior: Right after refresh window we see a sawtooth of 429 responses on /v1/chat/stream and /v1/embeddings endpoints. Throttles are biased towards connections that re-auth within the same 10s window. Token headers show different ephemeral values but are mapped to same tenant and route weights. Token/burst accounting indicates the tenant's burst pool is drained rapidly then slowly refills.
expected_behavior: Token refreshes should not cause tenant-level burst-pool exhaustion when aggregate sustained request rate is within committed capacity. Best-effort jittering and client reconnection strategies should avoid synchronized fanout creating transient 429s.
logs_and_evidence: 2026-03-10T15:00:18Z RATE-LIMITER INFO tenant=shf123 burst_pool=true route_smoothing=true refill_rate=10/s current_credit=0
Stacktrace snippets: rate-limiter metrics show spike at 15:00:12Z with concurrent reconnect count ~644 (expected ~620)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: synchronized SSO refresh causes fanout of short-lived tokens which are counted per-connection and drain the route burst pool faster than anticipated.
Confirmed that route_smoothing and the tenant-level burst pool are both enabled for this dedicated pool; smoothing keeps low-latency stream weight but still charges burst credits on reconnects.
Edge proxy (envoy) health-checks for connections were observed to re-initiate auth on reconnect which increments token accounting before steady-state requests begin.
Observed missing jitter in ShelfAI's refresh logic — refreshes happen without randomized offset, aligning many workers to the same second window.
Checked refill metrics: tenant burst pool refill is tuned conservatively (10 credits/s) and the reconnect wave consumes ~800 credits in <20s.
No evidence of serving-runtime overload (GPU utilization within expected), so problem is quota/burst pool accounting rather than compute saturation.
comments: Support (Priya): Thanks for the report, we've begun investigating. Can you share the client refresh cadence and number of workers per host?

Customer (ShelfAI - ops@sheIf.ai): Refresh is 15m, exactly on the quarter (0,15,30,45). ~50 worker pods, 12 websockets per pod. We can add jitter but concerned about race windows. See slack thread #support-shelfai: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345/abcde

SRE (Ethan): Reproduced in staging by forcing aligned refresh; rate-limiter metrics show burst_pool hit. Filing a follow-up GH issue to expose per-route transient-backoff counters. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/981
Support (Priya): Recommended immediate mitigation — add randomized jitter (0-30s) to client refresh; if needed, enable dedicated burst_pool reserve for this route while we analyze long-term config.
root_cause: Synchronized SSO token refresh created a reconnect storm that consumed the tenant-level burst credits faster than the configured refill rate. Route smoothing preserved low-latency weighting but did not prevent burst-accounting on connection/auth events, so the tenant burst pool transiently exhausted and began returning 429s.
resolution_notes: Applied mitigations: 1) Recommended and validated client-side jitter rollout to ShelfAI (staged 10s jitter, then 30s). 2) Temporarily increased burst_pool reserve for the affected route on the dedicated pool by +300 credits during customer peak windows. 3) Adjusted edge-proxy auth handshake to defer burst accounting until first non-auth application frame in staging (experiment).
verification_steps: 1) ShelfAI rolled out 10-30s jitter to refresh cadence and monitored next two refresh cycles — 429s dropped from ~9% to ~0.5% during windows.
2) Observed tenant_burst_remaining stayed above 120 credits during refill period after reserve increase.
3) Staging tests with deferred-accounting change show reduced credit consumption during reconnect spike (further validation required before prod roll).
time_to_resolution: Mitigation (jitter + reserve) implemented within 6 hours of ticket creation; full engineering follow-up scheduled.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to evaluate deferred-accounting for auth handshake in rate-limiter (GH issue opened).
2) Create a console alert for tenant burst pool drain spikes with per-route attribution (product/observability ticket).
3) Share client best-practices doc for SSO-backed short-lived tokens (support KB).
4) Postmortem draft if further recurrence observed during next two weeks.
follow_up_actions: ENG: rate-limiter team to review burst accounting semantics and PR for deferred-accounting (owner: @ethan).
DX: publish 'SSO refresh jitter' KB and example client snippets (owner: @amina).
SRE: consider increasing default burst_pool refill on some dedicated SKUs or expose tunable per-customer (owner: @marta).
